examples.en: That driver is so reckless.
Reckless driving causes accidents.
The dog suddenly started barking wildly.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 화가 나면 말투가 난폭해져요.
examples.en: When he gets angry, his way of speaking turns rough.

examples.ko: 난폭한 장면이 많아서 아이와 보기 힘들어요.
examples.en: There are many violent scenes, so it's hard to watch with a child.
We solve problems in a way that isn't violent.

explain: 행동이나 말투, 운전이 거칠고 사나워서 남에게 해를 줄 것 같을 때 써요. '거칠다'는 물건의 표면에도 쓰지만 난폭하다는 사람이나 동물의 행동에 주로 써요. 뉴스에서 '난폭 운전'이라는 말로 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It is used when actions, speech or driving are rough and fierce enough that they might harm others. '거칠다' can also describe a surface, but 난폭하다 is mainly used for the behavior of people or animals. You often see it in the news as '난폭 운전' (reckless driving).

examples.en: The baby has chubby cheeks and looks lovely and fortunate.

examples.ko: 복스럽게 밥을 먹는 모습이 보기 좋아요.
examples.en: It's nice to watch her eat so heartily.

examples.ko: 복스러운 얼굴이라 첫인상이 좋다는 말을 들어요.
examples.en: With her kind, full face, people say she makes a good first impression.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 웃는 모습이 정말 복스러웠어요.
examples.en: That child's smile looked really sweet and lucky.
A customer with a warm, generous look came into the shop.

examples.ko: 할머니는 복스럽다고 하시면서 제 볼을 만지셨어요.
examples.en: Grandma said I looked lovely and touched my cheek.

explain: 복이 있어 보이게 통통하고 넉넉한 인상이나, 맛있게 먹는 모습을 칭찬할 때 써요. 아기나 젊은 사람에게 어른이 하는 말로 자주 들어요. 외모를 평가하는 말이라 듣는 사람에 따라 불편할 수 있으니 조심하세요.
explain_en: It praises a plump, generous-looking, fortunate impression, or someone eating heartily. You often hear elders say it to babies and young people. Since it comments on appearance, it may bother some listeners, so be careful.

examples.en: This outfit is unsuitable for an interview.
It's an unsuitable movie for children.
That place was unsuitable for a gathering.
The weather is bad, so it's unsuitable and dangerous for hiking.
If you think it's inappropriate, please say so.

examples.ko: 이 재료는 요리에 부적당해서 쓰지 않아요.
examples.en: This ingredient is unsuitable for cooking, so we don't use it.

explain: '알맞다', '적당하다'의 반대쪽 말이에요. 말투가 딱딱해서 안내문, 심사, 서류에서 자주 나와요. 일상에서는 '안 어울려요', '안 맞아요'라고 말하는 경우가 더 많아요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of 적당하다 (suitable). The tone is formal, so it shows up in notices, evaluations, and documents. In daily talk people more often say 안 어울려요 or 안 맞아요.

examples.en: Water is indispensable to life.
Exercise is an indispensable habit for your health.
I threw away the things that weren't essential.
I think mobile phones are indispensable for modern people.
I want to become an indispensable person at my company.

examples.ko: 이 부품은 기계에 불가결해서 꼭 있어야 해요.
examples.en: This part is indispensable to the machine, so it must be there.

explain: 주로 '필수불가결하다'라는 형태로 많이 쓰고, 뉴스나 글에서 자주 나와요. 말할 때는 '꼭 필요하다'가 더 자연스러워요. '없어서는 안 되는'과 같은 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is most often used in the form '필수불가결하다' and appears often in news and writing. In speech, '꼭 필요하다' sounds more natural. It feels like 'cannot be done without'.

examples.ko: 불필요한 지출을 줄이려고 구독 서비스를 몇 개 해지했어요.
examples.en: To cut unnecessary spending, I canceled a few subscription services.

examples.ko: 선배가 보고서에서 불필요한 문장을 많이 줄여 줬어요.
examples.en: My senior cut a lot of unnecessary sentences from the report.
That explanation is unnecessary, so you can leave it out.
Leave the unneeded baggage at home.

examples.ko: 이 단계는 불필요하지 않아요. 꼭 해야 해요.
examples.en: This step is not unnecessary. You have to do it.
If you think it's unnecessary, please tell me right away.

explain: 반의어는 '필요하다'예요. 말할 때는 '필요 없다'가 더 자연스럽고, '불필요하다'는 글이나 설명, 회의 같은 자리에서 더 많이 들려요. '쓸데없다'는 더 부정적이고 감정이 들어간 말이에요.
explain_en: The opposite is '필요하다'. In speech '필요 없다' sounds more natural, while '불필요하다' is more common in writing, explanations and meetings. '쓸데없다' is more negative and emotional.

examples.ko: 심판은 인정사정 봐주지 않고 반칙을 불었어요.
examples.en: The referee called the foul without any mercy.

examples.ko: 장사할 때는 인정사정 따지면 손해를 봐요.
examples.en: In business, if you let sympathy get in the way, you lose money.

examples.ko: 이번에는 인정사정 보지 말고 규칙대로 해요.
examples.en: This time, let's follow the rules without going easy.
Don't expect any mercy from that person.
I asked them to go easy on me, but it was no use.

examples.ko: 인정사정 가리지 않고 일하다 보니 적이 많아졌어요.
examples.en: Working with no regard for sentiment, I made many enemies.

explain: '인정사정 봐주다/보다/없다'처럼 거의 '봐주지 않는다'는 뜻의 부정적인 표현과 함께 나와요. '인정사정없다'로 한 단어가 되기도 해요.
explain_en: It nearly always appears in expressions like '인정사정 봐주다/보다/없다', often about not going easy on someone. It also forms the single adjective '인정사정없다'.
